newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle lightly sell at $69 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle lightly sell at $69 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $69.00 per cwt in light volume, steady with Wednesday and $3.00 higher than last week's top price, feedlot sources said.

About 900 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area Thursday, bringing the week-to-date figure to 113,800 including 20,900 formulated and 800 previously contracted cattle to be shipped this week and 300 or 8 loads of CME delivery cattle, USDA said.
About 1,300 head sold in Kansas, which brought weekly sales to 92,400 including 17,500 or about 19 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.
Feedlot cattle prices this week were supported by strong beef prices and tight market-ready cattle supplies, feedlot sources said.
Heavyweight choice beef prices at midday were quoted up $1.28 per cwt at $105.90, USDA said. That prices was up $8.52 a week ago and the highest level since Dec 31, USDA statistics showed.

A few loads of cattle sold at $70.00 in western Nebraska on Wednesday, which generated expectations that feedlot sales in the Panhandle and Kansas would also be at $70.00 next week, Kansas and Texas cattle feeders said.
